title: Intel 4004, an early single-chip microprocessor
summary: Intel released the 4004, a 4-bit computer processor on a single chip, first used in Busicom calculators: the first significant commercial example of large-scale integration of a CPU.
why: Put a computer's processor on one chip that anyone could buy.

notes.problem: Source says 'first commercial microprocessor available for general use' (Four-Phase AL1 was in a product earlier); 'Santa Clara' is today's HQ, not given by source for 1971.
Bare 'first commercial microprocessor' overreaches: source says 4004 was first 'available for general use' and Four-Phase AL1 was first in a commercial product; 'made PCs possible' overclaims.
Source does not say 'first microprocessor sold for general use' (priority is contested by other 1969-71 chips); it says 'the first significant commercial example of large-scale integration'.
